card.name: Odd breaks inside labels and cross-references
card.fires_on: Short pieces in drug-label text that sit inside a split-up word, a brand name, a confidence-interval abbreviation, or a section cross-reference. Examples are the CI in 95% CI, the CY in UNLOXCYT, and the punctuation after PRECAUTIONS.

modes.label: Split brand or table words
modes.description: Pieces inside a spaced-out or brand word such as UNLOXCYT or a table header.
modes.example: UNLOX<<CY>>T can cause immune-mediated hepatitis, defined

modes.label: CI in statistics
modes.description: The abbreviation CI inside a 95% confidence interval.

modes.label: Cross-reference punctuation
modes.description: A bracket, comma or colon right after a section name like PRECAUTIONS or CONTRAINDICATIONS.
modes.example: Refer to PRECAUTIONS<< ,>> Drug Interactions for further information
